finding.claim: Removing the zero floor of avail_hp at thermal_model.py:2581 survives the full gate; 1275 of 17496 ordinary-dt grid inputs change the delivery (max abs diff 2.72 kW).
finding.mechanism: With a negative availability (heat-pump input below standing loss and the tank at the floor), the floor keeps the draw non-negative; unpinned, a negative hp_draw makes the tank gain heat from the emitters.

gate_survivors.patch: hp_draw = min(drawn - wood_draw, max(avail_hp, 0.0)) -> hp_draw = (drawn - wood_draw)
gate_survivors.should_fail: tests/optimality.py / features.py two-tank closures lack an assertion that a starved heat-pump tank cannot deliver more than it holds

finding.title: No check pins the availability cap on the two-tank heat-pump-tank draw
finding.claim: Replacing the min(drawn - wood_draw, max(avail_hp,0)) cap at thermal_model.py:2581 by drawn - wood_draw survives the full gate; 1280 of 17496 ordinary-dt grid inputs change the delivery (max abs diff 17.5 kW).
finding.mechanism: The energy bound that keeps the tank from delivering heat it does not hold is the only thing capping hp_draw; no check starves the heat-pump tank while the wood tank is also short.

gate_survivors.should_fail: tests/optimality.py / features.py two-tank closures lack an assertion that a partly starved step scales the emitter draw to delivered/drawn

finding.title: No check pins the proportional starvation scale of the two-tank draw
finding.claim: Removing the `drawn > delivered > 0.0` scaling branch at thermal_model.py:2583 survives the full gate; 1223 of 17496 ordinary-dt grid inputs change the emitter deliveries (max abs diff 16.9 kW).
finding.mechanism: The branch scales emitter deliveries down when the tanks can back only part of the draw; unpinned, the emitters are credited heat that no tank gave.
